Contrastive-loss research distinguishes relative negative penalties from shared gradient scaling ([Wang & Liu](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2021/papers/Wang_Understanding_the_Behaviour_of_Contrastive_Loss_CVPR_2021_paper.pdf); [Decoupled Contrastive Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.06848)). For the specified detached weights, direct differentiation gives: let d_j=n_j−p, S=Σ_j w_j exp(d_j), M=S/(1+S), and q_j=w_j exp(d_j)/S. Then ∂L/∂n_j=Mq_j and ∂L/∂p=−M. Thus q describes allocation, M aggregate negative-gradient mass, and total absolute logit-gradient mass is 2M. Equal weight sums do not fix S or M. Parameter gradients are MΣ_j q_j(∇θn_j−∇θp); their norms also depend on Jacobian alignment and cancellation.

Proposed controlled ablations: baseline, full weighting, allocation-only, and pressure-only. At identical parameters and candidates, compute baseline mass M₀ and weighted mass M_w. Multiply each weighted example loss by stopgrad(M₀/M_w) to retain weighted allocation with baseline mass; multiply baseline loss by stopgrad(M_w/M₀) to retain baseline allocation with weighted mass. Apply scaling before batch reduction. Measure allocation entropy/top-k share, M distributions, per-example and batch parameter-gradient norms, gradient cosine similarity, clipping frequency, and actual optimizer-update norms. Add a separate batch-gradient-norm-matched comparison; matching logit mass cannot guarantee matching parameter norms or Adam updates.

For timing, compare early, delayed, and shuffled intervention windows with identical active-step counts, strength schedules, total updates, learning-rate schedules, and sampled inputs. Curriculum research motivates random-order controls ([When Do Curricula Work?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.03107)). Match cumulative prescribed exposure; separately report cumulative realized allocation change, excess mass, and update norms because these depend on trajectory. Keep seed 42 and evaluate each single-model variant using fixed macro validation HR@10.
